request.content: # Requirement Analysis for Paywall Middleware in Proxmox VE Container Leasingnn## 1. Introductionnn### 1.1 Purpose of the DocumentnThis document defines the comprehensive set of requirements and constraints for developing a paywall middleware system that manages container leasing on a Proxmox VE infrastructure.nn### 1.2 Scope of the SystemnThe system is designed to authenticate users, manage leases for containers with detailed system specs, and directly interact with Proxmox VE API to provision and control container lifecycle. It enforces leasing rules such as lease expirations denying user access.nn## 2. Actors and Rolesnn### 2.1 Adminn- System administrators with full control over user management, lease provisioning, container lifecycle management, and system settings.nn### 2.2 Usern- Authenticated users who lease containers and manage their own leases, including viewing container specs and lease status.nn### 2.3 Authentication Mechanismsn- Basic authentication tying users to leased containers.nn## 3. Functional Requirementsnn### 3.1 User Registration and Authenticationn- Support for basic user authentication with role-based access control (admin, user).nn### 3.2 Container Leasing Managementn- Lease Creation: Ability for users/admin to request a new container lease. System obtains next available VMID from Proxmox VE and provisions container.n- Lease Renewal: Users can renew leases before or after expiry; middleware verifies container status and starts container if stopped.n- Lease Expiry: Automatic detection and denial of access if the lease has expired. System stops container if required.nn### 3.3 Container Lifecycle Managementn- Direct interaction with Proxmox VE API endpoints for cluster operations including create, start, stop, exec, vncproxy, and task status.nn### 3.4 API Endpoints and Actionsn- POST /lease/container: Create Leasen- POST /lease/{ctid}/renew: Renew Leasen- GET /management/list: List User Containersn- POST /management/exec/{ctid}: Run Commandn- POST /management/console/{ctid}: Get Console URLnn## 4. Business Rulesnn### 4.1 Lease Expirationn- Access denied to users on expired leases.nn### 4.2 Resource Specificationsn- Lease records must include lease end date, RAM, CPU, disk info associated with containers.nn### 4.3 Permissionsn- Admins have full control; users have restricted control limited to their own leases.nn## 5. Integration with Proxmox VEnn### 5.1 API Endpoint Interactionsn- Utilize provided Proxmox endpoints for cluster next ID, LXC creation, status management, command execution, VNC access, and task monitoring.nn### 5.2 Environment Variablesn- Required .env variables include PVE_HOST, PVE_TOKEN_ID, PVE_TOKEN_SECRET, PVE_NODE, PVE_STORAGE, PVE_OS_TEMPLATE, PVE_ROOT_PASSWORD, PVE_VERIFY_SSL.nn### 5.3 API Permissionsn- Token must have permissions like PVEVMAdmin, Datastore.AllocateSpace.nn## 6. Security Considerationsnn### 6.1 Authentication Securityn- Secure basic auth and token validation.nn### 6.2 Authorizationn- Role-based access controls.nn## 7. API Detailsnn- Detailed API routes with methods and respective proxmox API mappings.nn## 8. Future Expansionnn- Placeholder for implementing x402 payment protocol for actual payments and enforcement.nn## 9. Appendicesnn- Glossary of termsn- References to Proxmox VE documentation and API specsnn---nnThis requirement analysis reflects all provided inputs and adheres to the purpose of guiding backend developers in building the middleware.
